canonical.sourceFilePath: 06.Bit Manipulation/3. Advanced Maths/04. Prime factorization using Sieve.cpp

narrative.title: Decomposing the Alloy Into Its Base Metals
narrative.scenario: A foundry receives an alloy batch identified by an integer and must list every base-metal unit that composes it — prime factors with multiplicity, so a doubled component appears twice. The factor-sieve marks shared-access values as it goes, and every surviving prime is divided out of the batch repeatedly, one entry per removal, until nothing but 1 remains.
narrative.outputFormat: The prime factors of n with multiplicity, in non-decreasing order.

complexity.optimalTime: O(sqrt(n)) for the trial sweep; the sieve array makes it O(n log log n) as written

testCases.explanation: The 2-component occurs squared, so it is listed twice.

hintLevels: Level 1: Unlike distinct-factor listing, multiplicity matters — divide each prime out repeatedly and record every removal.
Level 2: For each surviving sieve prime i while i * i <= n, append and divide n by i in a while loop.
Level 3: The loop ends with n either 1 or a single large prime; that survivor is the final entry.
